newsitem.title: USA: Dallas pension fund has shortfall - state agency.
newsitem.headline: Dallas pension fund has shortfall - state agency.

text.p: Dallas' $1.3 billion employee pension fund has a funding shortfall that could pose a problem over the long term, the chairman of Texas' State Pension Review Board said Tuesday.

Don Reynolds, who chairs the oversight agency, said it reviewed the accounts at the request of the trustees of the Employee Retirement Fund, who maintain the shortfall is as much as $21 million annually.
Reynolds declined to put a figure on the shortfall. "It is difficult to quantify, but I feel strongly that there is underfunding that could pose a problem over the long-term."
City officials denied the claim, insisting that the fund is in good shape.
Assistant City Manager Mary Suhm said the pension board conducted a review but not a full-blown actuarial analysis. She said the city hired actuaries who found no problems.
"There is no problem with the fund," Suhm said. "I'm a 20-year-old employee and am comfortable. If I weren't, you would be hearing about it."
Suhm said the pension fund's investments in the past 12 years have earned an average annual return of more than 12 percent, way above the 8.25 percent return assumed by the fund in its projections.

City employees currently contribute 5 percent of their salary into the fund and the city puts up 8.5 percent. Some of the fund's trustees have said the city or its employees should increase their contribution to avoid a collapse.
They have claimed the fund could collapse in about 30 years if the funding issue is not resolved. Any increase in the city's contribution would require approval by voters.
The State Pension Review Board is to make its report on the fund's finances public next month.
Dennis E. Porcaro, vice-president at Moody's Investor Service in Dallas, said he has been aware of the issue, but is not concerned for the moment.
"This is a political issue and must be resolved among themselves. We will, however, continue to watch the situation," Porcaro said. --U.S. Municipal Desk, 212-859-1650
